reviews.body:
Read the head (`46c0efb7`), not just the diff. The core of the change holds: a falsy first argument emits `CONSOLE_ERROR` with the `Assertion failed` prefix DevTools prints, a passing assert emits nothing, `level: "error"` in the evaluator already accepts `CONSOLE_ERROR` (`engine/src/question/predicate/predicate-console.ts:78,85`), so `reticle_assert({ kind: "console", level: "error", absent: true })` now sees a failed assertion. The teardown identity assertion is a good addition.

Two things, neither blocking merge.

**1. `assert` is now a REQUIRED patch, and the failure mode is a half-installed observer.**

`assert` was added to the loop at `adapters/realm/browser/src/observers/console.ts:92`, and every iteration calls `requireCapturedMethod` (`console.ts:116`), which throws when the property is not an own value (`util/captured-method.ts:42-46`). For the five original methods that contract was safe: no page that has a `console` at all is missing `console.error`. The sixth is different, because a page can replace `window.console` with a shim that implements the five and not `assert`, and that is the one shape where the new requirement fails.

The throw lands on the last iteration, after `log`/`warn`/`error`/`info`/`debug` are already assigned (`console.ts:139`), and before the window listeners are registered (`console.ts:249`). `guard` then catches it and returns an empty teardown (`observers/install-all.ts:44`), so nothing can undo the five wrappers. The page is left emitting `CONSOLE_*` events, with no uncaught-error, rejection or CSP capture, and a `console` that stays patched for the life of the document.

Options, in the order I would pick them: skip a method whose own value is absent, keeping the five required (the loop already has the descriptor read in hand); or patch `assert` after the loop with a fallback that only emits when the original exists. A test with a five-method console shim and an assertion that the error listener still fires would pin it.

**2. The `gate` job is red for a non-defect reason.** `gate` exited 1 on `a required gate reported 'abandoned'`: the dependency results list contains `abandoned`, which the script treats as fatal. That is a cancelled dependency run rather than a failing check, so a workflow re-run should clear it. Flagging it only so the red row does not look like something in this diff.

Thank you for the quick fix. It addresses the review. One small ask:

1. Rename `.changes/c4402-console-assert.md` to `.changes/console-assert-error.md`, or to `<issue>-console-assert.md` if an issue exists, and link that issue.

comments.body: Thanks for your first pull request to Reticle! A maintainer aims to review within two days. Before then, `pnpm verify` locally catches most of what CI will, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reticlehq/reticle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the rest. If CI does not start, a maintainer needs to approve it for first-time contributors; that is normal.

Thanks for the careful read. Pushed two commits: the first skips `assert` when the console has no own `assert` value (the five original methods stay required), so the observer no longer half-installs on a five-method console shim. The second extends the shim test to dispatch an `ErrorEvent` and check that the uncaught-error listener still fires. With `assert` removed, install does not throw, `console.error` is still captured, and teardown restores the methods. The red `gate` row looks like a cancelled dependency run, as noted; a re-run should clear it.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
